newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Brash accepts mkts will go as far as RBNZ allows.
newsitem.headline: Brash accepts mkts will go as far as RBNZ allows.

text.p: Reserve Bank of New Zealand Governor Don Brash told a parliamentary committee on Wednesday he agreed that financial markets consider monetary conditions to be tight and the market would try to ease as much as the bank would allow.
Brash was giving testimony on the bank's June Monetary Policy Statement to the Finance and Expenditure Select Committee.

Asked by Labour Party Finance Spokesman Michael Cullen if the market's response to the MPS on Friday to loosen conditions to the extremity of the bank's tolerance level suggested that markets considered conditions tight, and they would go as far as the bank would allow, Brash said: "Yes, that is a reasonable inference."
The bank said it wanted monetary conditions to average 825 in the September quarter on its Monetary Conditions Index but it would tolerate conditions 50 points either side of that.
During Wednesday morning the MCI moved below 775, dipping to 760 by 9.50 a.m. (2150 GMT).
